name: Kurama to Kibune over Mount Kurama (鞍馬・貴船)
why: A temple mountain north of Kyoto: up past the halls of Kurama-dera, over a ridge of tangled cedar roots where the tengu goblins are said to live, and down to the shrine of the water god in a cool river valley.
book: Kurama-dera asks 500 yen at the gate; open 9:00-16:15. The cable car (200 yen) saves half the climb. Eizan railway from Demachiyanagi to Kurama, 30-40 minutes; from Kibune walk or take the bus to Kibuneguchi station.
water: Drinks and toilets in Kurama village, at the main hall and in Kibune. Kibune's riverside restaurants serve lunch on platforms over the river in summer.
dangers: Roots and stone steps on the Kinone-michi ridge: slippery in rain.
Summer humidity on the climb to the main hall.
Snow and ice on the ridge after winter cold spells.
turnaround: The temple closes its gates at 16:15: start the walk by 14:00 or go down the way you came.

points.name: Kurama-dera
points.note: The red Niomon gate above Kurama station. Climb the zigzag path past Yuki shrine and its giant cedars, or take the cable car.

points.name: Kurama-dera main hall
points.note: The main hall on its terrace, 30-45 minutes up, with the view over the northern hills. The path to Kibune leaves behind it.

points.name: Okunoin Maoden
points.note: The inner hall of the demon king Maoson, past the root-covered Kinone-michi; from here steep steps drop to the west gate.

points.name: Kibune shrine
points.note: Across the river from the west gate: the lantern-lined steps up to the main shrine of the water god.
